module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Cunningham chains — Jones's conjecture

A Cunningham chain is a sequence of primes satisfying either $p_{i+1}=2p_i+1$
(first kind) or $p_{i+1}=2p_i-1$ (second kind). It is conjectured that there
are infinitely many chains of every positive exact length, of both kinds.

A chain has **exact length k** when its first $k$ terms are prime and the
$(k+1)$-th generated term is composite.

Lenny Jones conjectures that for every positive integer $k$, infinitely many
primes start a chain of exact length $k$, for each of the two kinds.

*References:*
- Lenny Jones, [Polynomial Cunningham Chains](https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.1579)
- [OEIS A181697](https://oeis.org/A181697), first-kind chain lengths
- [OEIS A181715](https://oeis.org/A181715), second-kind chain lengths
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace CunninghamChain

/-- The `n`th term generated from `p` by the first-kind recurrence `q ↦ 2q + 1`. -/
def firstKindTerm (p : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ
  | 0     => p
  | n + 1 => 2 * firstKindTerm p n + 1

/-- The `n`th term generated from `p` by the second-kind recurrence `q ↦ 2q - 1`. -/
def secondKindTerm (p : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ
  | 0     => p
  | n + 1 => 2 * secondKindTerm p n - 1

/-- `p` starts a first-kind Cunningham chain of exact positive length `k`. -/
def IsFirstKindChainOfLength (p k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  0 < k ∧ (∀ i < k, (firstKindTerm p i).Prime) ∧ ¬(firstKindTerm p k).Prime

/-- `p` starts a second-kind Cunningham chain of exact positive length `k`. -/
def IsSecondKindChainOfLength (p k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  0 < k ∧ (∀ i < k, (secondKindTerm p i).Prime) ∧ ¬(secondKindTerm p k).Prime

-- Sanity-check: 2 starts a first-kind chain of length 5
-- (2, 5, 11, 23, 47 are prime; 2·47+1 = 95 = 5·19 is composite)
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem two_starts_firstKind_length_five : IsFirstKindChainOfLength 2 5 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, ?_, by norm_num [firstKindTerm]⟩
  intro i hi
  interval_cases i <;> norm_num [firstKindTerm]

-- Sanity-check: 7 starts a second-kind chain of length 2
-- (7, 13 are prime; 2·13-1 = 25 = 5² is composite)
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem seven_starts_secondKind_length_two : IsSecondKindChainOfLength 7 2 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, ?_, by norm_num [secondKindTerm]⟩
  intro i hi
  interval_cases i <;> norm_num [secondKindTerm]

/--
Jones's conjecture (first kind): for every positive integer $k$, there are
infinitely many primes $p$ that start a first-kind Cunningham chain of
exactly length $k$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinitely_many_firstKind_chains (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) :
    Set.Infinite {p : ℕ | IsFirstKindChainOfLength p k} := by
  sorry

/--
Jones's conjecture (second kind): for every positive integer $k$, there are
infinitely many primes $p$ that start a second-kind Cunningham chain of
exactly length $k$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinitely_many_secondKind_chains (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) :
    Set.Infinite {p : ℕ | IsSecondKindChainOfLength p k} := by
  sorry

end CunninghamChain

reformulations.difference: The source defines length as the least positive iteration producing a composite. Lean instead requires a positive length k, primality at every index i < k, and nonprimality at index k.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Index 0 and k > 0 force the starting number p to be prime. Every generated term is therefore at least 2, so nonprimality is equivalent to compositeness. The preceding-prime condition is exactly the minimality of the stopping index. In scratch.lean, first_exact_iff_source proves equivalence to p.Prime together with IsLeast {i | 0 < i ∧ Composite (firstKindTerm p i)} k, where Composite means having a divisor d with 2 ≤ d < the number.

reformulations.difference: As for the first kind, Lean uses a prime prefix followed by a nonprime term instead of the source's least positive composite stopping index; its recurrence also uses subtraction in ℕ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The predicate forces p to be prime, hence p ≥ 2. Induction shows every second-kind term is at least 2, so subtraction never truncates and a nonprime terminal term is genuinely composite. In scratch.lean, second_exact_iff_source proves equivalence to p.Prime together with the least-positive-composite stopping condition. The agreement of the recurrence with integer subtraction was also proved.

sources_consulted: Lenny Jones, Polynomial Cunningham Chains, arXiv:1104.1579v1, Definition 1.1 and the integer-chain conjecture in Section 1; polynomial results and concluding remarks: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1104.1579
OEIS A181697, read through the OEIS data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A181/A181697.seq
OEIS A181715, read through the OEIS data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A181/A181715.seq
review.notes: Checked all eight declarations. Both infinitude statements faithfully express the integer conjecture in Jones's introduction, not the polynomial analogue proved in the paper. Counting starting primes counts chains because the recurrence uniquely determines each chain. No left-maximality condition is required by Jones's definition or the cited OEIS sequences. Lean checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean cover k = 0 and 1, excluded starts 0 and 1, both sanity-check examples, the OEIS closed forms, and lengths for all primes below 60. The equivalence proofs do not depend on sorry axioms. Direct OEIS pages were browser-challenged; their entries were read through the data mirror.
